prompt: Write a Python function `roman_to_int(s: str) -> int` that converts a valid Roman numeral string `s` (using symbols I, V, X, L, C, D, M, value range 1 to 3999) to an integer. Subtractive notation applies: IV is 4, IX is 9, XL is 40, XC is 90, CD is 400, CM is 900.
title: Roman to Integer

prompt: Write a Python function `longest_common_prefix(strs: list[str]) -> str` that returns the longest common prefix string shared by all strings in `strs`. Return an empty string if there is no common prefix or if `strs` is empty.
title: Longest Common Prefix

prompt: Write a Python function `contains_nearby_duplicate(nums: list[int], k: int) -> bool` that returns True if there exist two distinct indices i and j such that nums[i] == nums[j] and abs(i - j) <= k, and False otherwise.
title: Contains Duplicate Within Distance K

prompt: Write a Python function `first_unique_char(s: str) -> int` that returns the index of the first non-repeating character in `s`, or -1 if no such character exists.
title: First Unique Character in a String

prompt: Write a Python function `group_anagrams(strs: list[str]) -> list[list[str]]` that groups the strings in `strs` so that strings that are anagrams of each other end up in the same group. Return the groups in any order.
test_cases: assert sorted([sorted(g) for g in group_anagrams(['eat', 'tea', 'tan', 'ate', 'nat', 'bat'])]) == sorted([['ate', 'eat', 'tea'], ['bat'], ['nat', 'tan']])
assert sorted([sorted(g) for g in group_anagrams(['abc', 'bca', 'cab', 'xyz', 'zyx'])]) == sorted([['abc', 'bca', 'cab'], ['xyz', 'zyx']])
title: Group Anagrams

prompt: Write a Python function `top_k_frequent(nums: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]` that returns the `k` most frequent elements in `nums`, in any order. It is guaranteed that the answer is unique in terms of which elements qualify (no ties at the cutoff), and 1 <= k <= number of unique elements.
title: Top K Frequent Elements

prompt: Write a Python function `product_except_self(nums: list[int]) -> list[int]` that returns an array `answer` where answer[i] is the product of all elements of `nums` except nums[i]. Do not use division. For a single-element input, return [1] (the product of no elements).
title: Product of Array Except Self

prompt: Implement a stack class `MinStack` in Python with methods `push(val: int) -> None`, `pop() -> None` (removes the top element), `top() -> int` (returns the top element), and `get_min() -> int` (returns the minimum element in the stack). All operations will be called on non-empty stacks where a return value is required.
test_cases: s = MinStack(); s.push(-2); s.push(0); s.push(-3); assert s.get_min() == -3
s = MinStack(); s.push(-2); s.push(0); s.push(-3); s.pop(); assert s.top() == 0; assert s.get_min() == -2
s = MinStack(); s.push(5); s.push(1); s.push(5); assert s.top() == 5; s.pop(); assert s.get_min() == 1
s = MinStack(); s.push(2); s.push(2); s.pop(); assert s.get_min() == 2
s = MinStack(); s.push(0); s.push(1); s.push(0); assert s.get_min() == 0; s.pop(); assert s.get_min() == 0
title: Min Stack

prompt: Write a Python function `length_of_longest_substring(s: str) -> int` that returns the length of the longest substring of `s` without repeating characters.
title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters

prompt: Write a Python function `coin_change(coins: list[int], amount: int) -> int` that returns the fewest number of coins needed to make up `amount` using coins of the given denominations (unlimited supply of each). Return -1 if the amount cannot be made up, and 0 if amount is 0.
title: Coin Change (Fewest Coins)
